item.title: Port Moresby to face weekend water rationing as court orders unblock critical pipeline repairs
item.description: Water PNG has secured interim National Court orders to proceed with urgent repairs on a primary water pipeline supplying Port Moresby, following a land access dispute that delayed initial works. The National Court at Waigani issued orders restraining the Behori Incorporated Land Group, its members, and agents from blocking access to the Rouna 1/3 raw water pipeline.
item.content:encoded:
Water PNG has secured interim National Court orders to proceed with urgent repairs on a primary water pipeline supplying Port Moresby, following a land access dispute that delayed initial works.

The National Court at Waigani issued orders restraining the Behori Incorporated Land Group, its members, and agents from blocking access to the Rouna 1/3 raw water pipeline.

The critical infrastructure carries approximately half of the capital city's raw water supply. The ruling clears the way for a major partial shutdown of Port Moresby's water supply, now scheduled to run from 10:00pm on Friday, 14 August until 3:00am on Sunday, 16 August.

Water PNG Chief Executive Officer James Young said the city's water supply will be reduced by around half during the repair window, with water rationed across four zones on eight-hour rotations.

"This repair is about preventing something far worse," Young said. "The pipeline is more than sixty years old and it is failing.

"A short, planned, partial shutdown now is how we avoid an uncontrolled burst later, one that could cut more than half the city's water not for a weekend, but for weeks or months, because no spare pipe of this size is held in the country."

Engineers estimate the current leak is losing around 10 million litres of water every day.

Officials warned the wastage poses an immediate risk during an active El Niño period, which is already placing pressure on the Sirinumu catchment - the region's primary source for both drinking water and hydropower.

Water PNG board chairman Meckles Poya welcomed the court's intervention while reaffirming the State Owned Enterprise's intention to maintain a long-term working relationship with traditional landowners.

"We respect the Behori Clan and their deep connection to their land, and at the same time Water PNG has a responsibility under the law to make sure people have safe water," Poya said.

He said Behori-owned contractors had been engaged and paid for preparatory site works, including grading access roads and digging drainage channels, prior to a blockade being erected.

"If the water supply fails, disease can spread, people get sick, and lives can be lost who are often our most vulnerable, our children and the elderly," Poya said.

Water PNG confirmed that full support for the repair program and future pipeline renewal has been backed by the National Government and Kumul Consolidated Holdings.

Detailed zone rationing maps and schedules are expected to be published ahead of the August 14 shutdown.

item.title: North Fly police strengthened with new fleet
item.description: The Police Special Services Division in North Fly will now beef up security operations in the Tabubil mining area and surrounding communities after receiving three new police marked vehicles from Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML]. Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police for Border Command Steven Francis said the vehicles will improve police mobility, operational readiness, visibility and response time
item.content:encoded:
The Police Special Services Division in North Fly will now beef up security operations in the Tabubil mining area and surrounding communities after receiving three new police marked vehicles from Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML].

Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police for Border Command Steven Francis said the vehicles will improve police mobility, operational readiness, visibility and response times within Tabubil and the wider North Fly area.

The vehicles were officially handed over to police yesterday, and will be assigned to the Special Services Division, whose personnel are regularly deployed to support security operations within the mine’s operational areas.

"This occasion is not simply about the handover of three vehicles. It represents a broader commitment by OTML and the RPNGC Border Command to work together in addressing law-and-order challenges," ACP Francis said.

He said the donation was small but significant as it reflects the continuing strategic partnership between OTML and police.

ACP Francis acknowledged OTML for their continued support to the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary, particularly provincial commands within the Border Command.

ACP Francis said there has been positive progress through stronger cooperation between OTML, the North Fly Provincial Police Command and the wider RPNGC.

He urged commanders and supervisors to ensure the vehicles are properly registered, monitored, serviced and used only for authorised policing duties.

"These vehicles must be used wisely, maintained properly and deployed in the service of the people. They must not be misused or treated as personal property," he said.

"These assets belong to the people and communities of North Fly. Police officers are only the custodians, and we have a responsibility to protect, maintain and manage them properly."

He thanked OTML for recognising the importance of strengthening police mobility to maintain peace and support the secure operation of one of PNG’s major economic projects.

ACP Francis reaffirmed the Border Command’s commitment to working closely with OTML, communities, government agencies and other partners to improve law enforcement and public safety throughout North Fly and the wider Border Command.

item.title: PNG far below Commonwealth standard for female leaders, former minister says
item.description: PNG political pioneer Lady Carol Kidu is spearheading a national campaign to boost female representation in parliament, urging that the country remains critically short of Commonwealth standards for women in leadership. More than 200 people attended a one-day Citizenship Awareness workshop in Northern Province on Wednesday, as part of an initiative backed by the Australian National University [ANU
item.content:encoded:
PNG political pioneer Lady Carol Kidu is spearheading a national campaign to boost female representation in parliament, urging that the country remains critically short of Commonwealth standards for women in leadership.

More than 200 people attended a one-day Citizenship Awareness workshop in Northern Province on Wednesday, as part of an initiative backed by the Australian National University [ANU] under the Pacific Women in Leadership Program.

The program, run alongside the Civic Awareness Coordinating Team in Oro, aims to build an informed electorate ahead of the 2027 National General Elections.

Lady Kidu, a former cabinet minister and the lead facilitator for the workshops, said Papua New Guinea needed to move toward shared governance after five decades of independence.

"The main purpose is to try to increase the number of women in parliament," Lady Kidu said.

"The Commonwealth standard is 30 per cent women in parliament, and we are a Commonwealth nation… We are under two per cent women in parliament. We never have been [near that] in our history."

The workshop locations were selected using ANU research that identified electorates where female candidates achieved strong first-preference votes in previous elections.

The national roadshow has already visited West Sepik and East Sepik, with upcoming sessions planned for Manus and Milne Bay.

Lady Kidu said money politics and shifting cultural norms were a hurdle for prospective female MPs, but stressed that inclusive decision-making was essential for national progress.

"We need a balance. We need women's thinking, women's priorities, as well as men in there," she said.

"In traditional politics, women had power behind the scenes, and now people have this idea that it's just men… My aim is to give women a chance."

item.title: PNG-Australia partnership strengthens agricultural markets in Western Highlands
item.description: Fresh investment in market infrastructure is continuing to transform agricultural trade in Western Highlands, with the opening of the upgraded Holy Trinity College Market. The opening of the new Holy Trinity market is reinforcing the long-standing partnership between the PNG and Australian Governments to improve livelihoods for local farmers, particularly women vendors.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh investment in market infrastructure is continuing to transform agricultural trade in Western Highlands, with the opening of the upgraded Holy Trinity College Market.

The opening of the new Holy Trinity market is reinforcing the long-standing partnership between the PNG and Australian Governments to improve livelihoods for local farmers, particularly women vendors.

The Australian High Commission announced that the upgraded market now provides a modern covered selling area and a reliable water supply, giving hundreds of growers and vendors a safer, cleaner and more convenient place to sell their fresh produce.

The market also serves more than 1,000 students, staff and visitors from surrounding community educational institutions like the Holy Trinity Teachers College and Holy Trinity Demonstration Primary School.

Before the upgrade, vendors had little protection from sun and rain and no dependable water source.

The project has delivered a new market shelter and four water tanks providing a combined capacity of 9,000 litres, improving hygiene, food safety and creating a better trading environment.

Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea Ewen McDonald said the project demonstrates how locally led partnerships can deliver practical improvements for communities.

"Holy Trinity College Market is an important place for students, staff, families and local growers, especially women vendors who sell produce here each day to support their families. Through the partnership, Australia is pleased to support improvements that respond to local priorities and contribute to better services and stronger livelihoods," Mr McDonald said.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa welcomed Australia's continued investment, thanking the people and Government of Australia for their ongoing commitment to supporting agriculture and market infrastructure across the province.

Governor Rapa said the Holy Trinity College Market follows Australia's earlier support for the redevelopment of the Mt Hagen Main Market, further strengthening opportunities for rural farmers to earn sustainable incomes.

"On behalf of the people of Western Highlands Province, I sincerely thank the Government and people of Australia for continuing to invest in our province. Agriculture is the backbone of our economy, and quality market facilities give our farmers—especially our mothers and women vendors—a safe and dignified place to sell their produce.

From the redevelopment of the Mt Hagen Main Market to the Holy Trinity Satellite Market, Australia has been a trusted development partner," Governor Rapa said.

Rapa also highlighted that the Western Highlands Provincial Government contributed K1 million towards the province's community water security market program under the PNG–Australia Partnership (which is a K4.5million project), helping establish mini markets equipped with improved water facilities across the province.

"The Western Highlands Provincial Government proudly partnered with the PNG–Australia Partnership by contributing K1 million towards these community market and water security projects. Together we are creating mini markets that improve food security, boost local incomes and support economic growth in our rural communities," said the Western Highlands Governor.

The Holy Trinity Market upgrade is one of 14 water security structures completed across Western Highlands under the PNG–Australia Partnership, with the provincial government co-investing K1 million in the overall program.

Across Papua New Guinea, more than 200 water security projects have been delivered in markets and schools through the Australia Papua New Guinea Subnational Program.

item.title: PM Marape: ‘JSB meeting reached important step for PNG-Bougainville future today’
item.description: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape says a historic threshold has been reached in relations with Bougainville, following the formal end of joint consultations on the region's 2019 independence referendum. At a meeting of the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] at Melanesian Haus in Port Moresby, Mr Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama endorsed the Joint Consult
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape says a historic threshold has been reached in relations with Bougainville, following the formal end of joint consultations on the region's 2019 independence referendum.

At a meeting of the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] at Melanesian Haus in Port Moresby, Mr Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama endorsed the Joint Consultation Report and a new Melanesian Framework.

The agreement clears the way for the referendum results to be formally tabled on the floor of PNG's National Parliament on August 27.

Nearly 98 per cent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence from Papua New Guinea in the non-binding 2019 vote. Under the terms of the 2001 Peace Agreement, PNG's parliament retains the final decision on whether to grant full sovereignty.

Marape said the national government had met all its constitutional obligations and that MPs must now vote on the outcome according to conscience and the national interest.

"While we cannot rewind history, we must construct our future as a people," Marape said.

"The work since 2001 has seen many JSBs, many meetings, many exchanges, that has culminated in the implementation of Section 338 of our National Constitution as far as calling a referendum is concerned."

He emphasised that the upcoming parliamentary vote would not mark an end to ties between PNG and the autonomous region, but represented the next phase in a 25-year peace process.

As part of the resolutions reached at the summit, the JSB agreed to hand over all locally generated revenue including taxes from fisheries, mining, forestry, and land, to the Bougainville government by December 31 this year to build the region's fiscal capacity.

Future political and administrative cooperation between Port Moresby and Buka will be managed under the Melanesian Framework.

Marape paid tribute to the patience of Bougainvilleans and urged calm across both regions as the matter moves into its parliamentary phase.

"The Peace Agreement clearly says parliament will determine the final result," he said.

"Section 342, subsection 2 says parliament will make this decision. Whatever that decision is to the people of Bougainville and Papua New Guinea, we must respect the parliament process.

"And that is not the end... the Speaker of the National Parliament then will pass the result and the decision to the Speaker of the Bougainville Parliament."

The Prime Minister called on citizens to pray for wisdom and unity, adding that PNG had demonstrated to the world how complex national questions could be resolved peacefully through constitutional democracy.

item.title: Gamai calls on LLG leaders to stay in communities as new chamber opens
item.description: The new Fly Gogodala local level government [LLG] chamber was officially opened on Monday at Tapila Station in the Delta Fly district of Western by local MP and Livestock Minister Agena Gamai. The decision to construct the chamber was passed in 2024 by members of the District Development Authority [DDA] board.
item.content:encoded:
The new Fly Gogodala local level government [LLG] chamber was officially opened on Monday at Tapila Station in the Delta Fly district of Western by local MP and Livestock Minister Agena Gamai.

The decision to construct the chamber was passed in 2024 by members of the District Development Authority [DDA] board.

The new facility will house local government operations and administration, bringing decision-making and service delivery closer to the rural population of Fly Gogodala.

Speaking during the opening ceremony, Gamai told the local community that following his election in 2022 as the pioneer Member for Delta Fly, his vision was to ensure that administrative operations were not concentrated solely at the district headquarters.

"My vision was to build the seat of government in all the LLG growth centres," Gamai said.

"Today marks the fulfillment of part of that vision that I had, and others will follow."

Gamai encouraged all LLG presidents to return to their respective areas and remain stationed with their people to ensure basic services reach the grassroots level.

The chamber opening was part of a broader community programme that also featured the official opening of a new Evangelical Church of Papua New Guinea [ECPNG] building to serve the spiritual needs of the Tapila community.

Additionally, a dinghy was presented to the Tapila Health Centre to support emergency transport and movement for health workers and patients in the riverine district.

The ceremony was witnessed by DDA members, LLG presidents for Tabo, Fly Gogodala, and Bamu, former Fly Gogodala leadership, as well as community members from Tapila and surrounding villages.

item.title: 18th Sepik River crocodile & arts festival kicks off
item.description: Festivities of the three-day show that promotes the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik River and draws visitors into East Sepik started today. The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival was officially opened this morning by Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk with a strong emphasis to improve tourism in the Sepik River region.
item.content:encoded:
Festivities of the three-day show that promotes the rich cultural heritage of the Sepik River and draws visitors into East Sepik started today.

The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival was officially opened this morning by Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk with a strong emphasis to improve tourism in the Sepik River region.

"We need to bring back the glory days of Ambunti, Angoram, Gawi, and Ambunti must collaborate and bring tourists back," Wiruk said.

"Tourism of cultural events has contributed to cultural, social, and economic development of the region."

Sharing similar sentiments, Provincial Minister of Culture and Tourism Godfrey Wakraai, revealed plans to revive dying cultures in the province.

Wakraai, the president of Gawanga LLG in Ambunti Drekikir district was among the dignitaries in attendance during the opening ceremony of the festival.

The 18th Sepik River Crocodile & Arts Festival rides under the theme 'Keeping and strengthening tourism through Arts, Culture, and Environment'.

The first day of activities showcased a variety of performances from different cultural groups from both Sepik River communities their neighbors - Wosera and Maprik.

The festival is sponsored by a number of groups including Frieda River Limited [FRL] - a partner that has been committed to supporting the show since 2011.

item.title: Western PHA prepares reporting system for province-wide immunisation campaign
item.description: The Western Provincial Health Authority is rolling out a new digital reporting system ahead of its province-wide Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign in August and September, with support from PNGSDP and World Vision PNG. A two-day Training of Trainers workshop concluded yesterday in Daru for South Fly District team leaders to equip them with skills to use the Digital Health Information Software
item.content:encoded:
The Western Provincial Health Authority is rolling out a new digital reporting system ahead of its province-wide Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign in August and September, with support from PNGSDP and World Vision PNG.

A two-day Training of Trainers workshop concluded yesterday in Daru for South Fly District team leaders to equip them with skills to use the Digital Health Information Software 2 [DHIS2], and the Kobo Collect tool.

The tools will be used to track progress and conduct surveys to identify factors contributing to low immunisation coverage.

Following the Daru training, team leaders will conduct facility-based training across South Fly District. The same training will be extended to other districts, with North Fly and Middle Fly districts scheduled for August 10th to 11th in Kiunga.

PNGSDP has supported the campaign with 86 Android tablets for 86 teams across the province. The tablets will be given to designated data capturers in each team to ensure data entry does not distract clinicians, who will focus on vaccinating children.

The digital system will help WPHA’s Monitoring and Evaluation teams keep accurate records of children immunised during the campaign.

The initial target group is children under one year of age. However, WPHA chief executive officer Dr. Miriam Boga said the campaign will also include older children following reports of a new measles outbreak in New Ireland Province.

"We have also made an exception to include older children as the country now reports a new measles outbreak in the New Ireland Province," Dr. Boga said.

Executive Manager for North Fly District Health Services Galeva Sere closed the Daru training and acknowledged partners for their technical support in developing the reporting framework WPHA will use.

The Catch-up Routine Immunisation Campaign is scheduled for North Fly and Middle Fly from August 17th-28th, and South Fly and Delta Fly from September 7th-18th.

item.title: JSB endorses consultation report, Bougainville referendum vote heads to National Parliament on August 27
item.description: The Joint Supervisory Body has formally endorsed the Post-Consultation Report and the Melanesian Agreement in Port Moresby today, clearing the path for the Bougainville referendum results to be tabled in the National Parliament on August 27.

item.title: New police fleet to strengthen operations across Northern Command
item.description: Police in Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands are set to benefit from a new fleet of vehicles under the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary's fleet replacement program.
